title: Acute prostatitis (infection of the prostate)

items: Acute prostatitis is a sudden infection of the prostate gland in men.
It can cause a fever and make passing urine difficult.
Pain in the perineum (between the legs), the lower back, or the pelvis.
Burning when passing urine, needing to pass urine often, and trouble emptying the bladder.
Urine test and urine culture before antibiotics.
Blood cultures if you have a fever or are unwell.
A bladder scan if you cannot pass urine.
Sexually transmitted infection tests if there is risk.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on the culture.
Your doctor will explain the plan after your test results.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not have a prostate massage or any rough examination; these can cause a serious infection to spread.
Your doctor may check your urine again after treatment, and review your symptoms.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Unable to pass urine at all
